prompt: A car travels $180$ miles in $3$ hours at a constant speed. What is its speed, in miles per hour?
hint: Speed in miles per hour tells how many miles are covered in one hour. Which operation shares the distance equally among the hours?

hints.text: Speed in miles per hour tells how many miles are covered in one hour. Which operation shares the distance equally among the hours?
Divide the total distance by the total time, which here is $180 \div 3$.
Since $180 \div 3 = 60$, the speed of the car is $60$ miles per hour.

learningObjective: Compute a unit rate from a total and a quantity.
explanation: A rate per hour is the total distance divided by the total time taken.
The car covers $180$ miles in $3$ hours, so the speed is $180 \div 3 = 60$.
Miles divided by hours gives miles per hour, so the speed is $60$ miles per hour.

alternativeExplanations.title: Let the units tell you the operation
steps: You want an answer in miles/hour — a fraction with miles on top and hours on the bottom.
So write $\dfrac{180 \text{ miles}}{3 \text{ hours}}$ and the operation is decided for you.
On any rate question, writing the target units first prevents dividing the wrong way round.
